items.title: IRGC claims attack on ship in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran says will attack any ship trying to pass through Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday that it struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, setting the ship on fire, according to a statement the IRGC provided to Report.az. The IRGC did not disclose the origin or purpose of the targeted vessel, though the attack follows a pattern of strikes Iran has described as targeting Israel-linked shipping in the Persian Gulf.[1]

The incident is the latest in a string of maritime attacks that have paralyzed one of the world's most important waterways since the United States and Israel launched military operations against Iran on February 28, bringing the five-week-old conflict to a critical juncture at sea.

featured_image.name: After Strait of Hormuz opens, turmoil would still last months, analysts ...

items.description: Recent U.S. intelligence assessments warn that Iran is unlikely to ease its chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz anytime soon, as control over the vital oil artery remains Tehran's primary leverage against Washington, Reuters reported Thursday, citing three sources familiar with the matter. items.description: China and Pakistan have launched a joint five-point peace initiative calling for an immediate ceasefire in the war on Iran, the most detailed proposal from a major global power since the conflict began on February 28. The plan, announced on March 31 after hours of talks in Beijing between Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, has been met with near-silence from Washington and no clear signal of engagement from Tehran.

items.title: Artemis II crew passes halfway point on voyage to the moon

featured_image.name: Dirt, a 1970s flag, a stuffie: What's inside the Orion spacecraft

items.description:
Three days after lifting off from Florida, the crew of NASA's Artemis II mission has crossed the halfway mark on humanity's first journey to the moon in more than half a century. As of Saturday morning, the Orion spacecraft — named "Integrity" by its crew — was more than 152,000 miles from Earth and closing in on its lunar destination, traveling at speeds exceeding 2,600 miles per hour.[1]

The four astronauts — NASA Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — launched aboard NASA's Space Launch System rocket from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B at 6:35 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 1. The liftoff marked the first piloted moonshot since Apollo 17 in December 1972.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Turkey confirms second ship crosses Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Three ships appear to enter Hormuz by new route along Oman coast

items.description:
A second Turkish-flagged ship has crossed the Strait of Hormuz, Turkey's Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu confirmed on Saturday, even as a fleet of Omani tankers charted a new route through the contested waterway that bypasses Iran's controlled corridor entirely.[1][2]

The developments mark a cautious expansion of traffic through the strait, which has seen a roughly 95 percent drop in daily vessel movements since the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the conflict on February 28. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps imposed a selective blockade around March 14, routing permitted ships through a checkpoint between the Iranian islands of Larak and Qeshm.[3][4][5]

items.title: Polymarket bets on $120 oil jump after Iran strikes Gulf

featured_image.name: WTI crude oil price flips Brent as Polymarket traders sees ...

items.description:
Oil prices surged to their highest levels since 2022 this week after Iran launched a fresh wave of strikes on Gulf energy infrastructure, sending prediction market bettors scrambling to price in the possibility of even steeper gains. On Polymarket, the implied probability that WTI crude will touch $120 per barrel at some point in April has climbed to 77%, according to the platform's live market data, up from 65% just days earlier.[1][2]

The repricing followed a dramatic escalation on Friday, April 3, when Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery — which has a capacity of 346,000 barrels per day — setting off fires across the facility. Kuwait also reported an Iranian attack that caused material damage to a power and water desalination plant. Separately, Abu Dhabi suspended operations at its largest natural gas processing facility after debris from a projectile interception sparked a fire, and Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted several drones.[3][4][5]
